checkpoint: 1 — how the screenshots stage starts the engine, next to how run-game.ps1 starts it

machine.gpu: OpenGL API 3.3.0 NVIDIA 577.09 - Compatibility - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop GPU

howTheComparisonWasMade.reading: Only verify.ps1 calls Initialize-VerificationTemporaryRoot. No other engine-starting script does.

sideBySide.aspect: engine resolution, version assert, NuGet source, tool profile
sideBySide.runGame: the same four calls in the same order (scripts/run-game.ps1:117-122)

sideBySide.aspect: number of windowed engine processes in a row
sideBySide.reading: Real difference, but not the cause: see evidence/184-cause.json, where one process reproduces the noise on its own.

sideBySide.verifyScreenshotsStage: overwritten in preflight with the resolved temporary root: $env:TEMP = $candidate; $env:TMP = $candidate (scripts/TemporaryRoot.ps1:238-239), where $candidate comes from -TemporaryRoot, then $env:DUNGEON_FORTRESS_TEMP, then TMP/TEMP (scripts/TemporaryRoot.ps1:24-50)
sideBySide.runGame: untouched — run-game.ps1 never dot-sources TemporaryRoot.ps1 and never reads DUNGEON_FORTRESS_TEMP
sideBySide.reading: This is the difference. Initialize-GodotRuntimeEnvironment builds the Godot runtime profile as [IO.Path]::GetTempPath() + \df-godot-<hash of repo root> (scripts/GodotTools.ps1:158-159), and GetTempPath reads TMP first. So the two scripts put user:// — and with it the GLES3 shader cache — in two different directories whenever a temporary-root override is in play.

theTwoProfilesOfTheReportedSession.note: Both directories are still on disk from the session that opened this Issue (worktree agent-a6060a8c77c1a0aec, evidence/77-pack-after.json states DUNGEON_FORTRESS_TEMP=.artifacts/tmp). Lengths are read off the filesystem, not computed.
theTwoProfilesOfTheReportedSession.command: powershell -NoProfile -Command "foreach ($r in @('C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\df-godot-630de8b0\Roaming','C:\gamedev\Dungeon fortress\.claude\worktrees\agent-a6060a8c77c1a0aec\.artifacts\tmp\df-godot-630de8b0\Roaming')) { $cache = (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath (Join-Path $r 'Godot\app_userdata') -Directory | Where-Object { $_.Name -like '*deterministic*' }).FullName; $dirs = Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath (Join-Path $cache 'shader_cache') -Directory | ForEach-Object { Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $_.FullName -Directory }; $lengths = @($dirs | ForEach-Object { $_.FullName.Length } | Sort-Object -Descending); '{0}  appDataLength={1}  shaderDirs={2}  lengths=[{3}]' -f $r, $r.Length, $lengths.Count, ($lengths -join ',') }"
theTwoProfilesOfTheReportedSession.reading: The same repository, the same engine, the same fourteen GLES3 shader classes, two profiles 69 characters apart. run-game.ps1 landed in the first (all fourteen cache directories 192-204 characters long, zero engine errors — .artifacts/probe-cold.log of that session). verify.ps1 landed in the second (all fourteen 261-273 characters long, fourteen ERROR lines — .artifacts/verify-probe.log of that session, lines 43-70).

whatIsNotTheDifference.claim: The frame the stage asks for.
whatIsNotTheDifference.refutedBy: evidence/77-pack-after.json, notTheGameArguments: the same frame through run-game.ps1 gives zero engine errors.

whatIsNotTheDifference.claim: The change under review at the time.
whatIsNotTheDifference.refutedBy: evidence/77-pack-after.json, notThisChange: the same failure on the pre-change tree.

whatIsNotTheDifference.claim: Three engine processes in a row rather than one.
whatIsNotTheDifference.refutedBy: evidence/184-cause.json: a single run-game.ps1 process reproduces the fourteen lines once its profile is long enough and its cache is warm.

openAtThisCheckpoint: Why a long profile path produces exactly these lines, and why the position of the noise moved between the reporter's three runs. Answered in evidence/184-cause.json.
